subject.title: fix(agents): add timeout to fd and ripgrep search executions

question: Should built-in find and grep enforce a fixed 60-second total-runtime deadline, or should they time out only after 60 seconds without search activity?
rationale: Both choices prevent indefinite hangs, but a total-runtime deadline can terminate legitimate large or remote-tree searches while an inactivity deadline requires slightly more lifecycle logic.

options.title: Use an inactivity deadline
options.body: Reset the 60-second deadline on meaningful helper output and force-terminate only when the search has made no progress for the full interval.

options.title: Keep the wall-clock deadline
options.body: Accept that all searches longer than 60 seconds fail, while still requiring definitive termination and cleanup before merge.

options.title: Defer the execution timeout
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers establish a shared timeout contract for built-in filesystem search tools.

recommendation.title: Use an inactivity deadline
recommendation.body: Reset the 60-second deadline on meaningful helper output and force-terminate only when the search has made no progress for the full interval.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work in adjacent agent child-process cancellation and settlement makes this the strongest available routing signal for the timeout-semantics choice.
